# getPath

<link-summary>Reads a nested property by path, with a fallback.</link-summary>

<web-summary>getPath() — Reads a nested property by path, with a fallback. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/object</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function getPath<T>(
  source: unknown,
  path: string | Array<string | number>,
  fallback?: T
): T | undefined;
```

The path is either a dotted string or an array of segments; array indices go in as numbers, as in `["rows", 0, "id"]`. Bracket syntax inside a string is **not** parsed — `"rows[0].id"` finds nothing.

A missing or nil link anywhere along the path yields the fallback instead of throwing, which is the whole point over `a.b.c`.

## Parameters

| Parameter               | Type                                | Description                                       |
| :---------------------- | :---------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------ |
| `source`                | `unknown`                           | The value to read from.                           |
| `path`                  | `string \| Array<string \| number>` | A dotted string, or an array of keys and indices. |
| `fallback` _(optional)_ | `T`                                 | Returned when the path does not resolve.          |

## Returns

`T | undefined` — the value at the path, or the fallback.

## Examples

### Reading

```javascript
getPath({ a: { b: 1 } }, "a.b"); // => 1
getPath({}, "a.b", "fallback"); // => "fallback"
getPath({ rows: [{ id: 7 }] }, ["rows", 0, "id"]); // => 7
```
